focus: P4 mutation API fence contract, atomic validation, resource/version coupling, and safe Graphene wave boundary
noveltyJustification: Iteration 6 proved the stale-successor hole; this pass closes P4 with an exact command envelope, per-resource fence/version coupling, a single authoritative commit rule, the cross-store atomicity limit, and an exhaustive boundary between Graphene planning evidence and 036 safety.
keyFindings: GraphMutationCommandV1 must explicitly carry exact claim, session, immutable claim version, operation identity, payload digest, and a complete ordered target set
Claim identity and the current monotonic resource fence are conjunctive proofs; neither substitutes for the other
Every target couples canonical resource identity, fence token, and expected state version or exact ledger head
Claim, all target fences, expected versions, idempotency, authorization, and transition rules must be revalidated in the same authoritative commit decision
Multi-resource fencing excludes stale writers but does not create crash atomicity across independent stores; use one authoritative ledger commit and derived views/effect intents
Every claim-derived completion, failure, retry, lease, checkpoint, status, salvage, budget, effect, and terminal mutation is claimant-addressed
Graphene read sets, readiness, claimability, stable claim IDs, budget checks, and deterministic folds may inform wave candidates but provide no durable write-safety certificate

ruledOut.reason: Fence authority is scoped to a canonical resource and cannot cover omitted or aliased targets

ruledOut.approach: Treat multi-resource mutex exclusion as a cross-store transaction
ruledOut.reason: Exclusion closes stale interleavings but cannot roll back partial independent persistence or external effects after crash

ruledOut.approach: Allow current-fence writes without an expected version or head
ruledOut.reason: A current owner can still overwrite a same-epoch concurrent change

ruledOut.approach: Use Graphene readiness or claim admission as a write-wave certificate
ruledOut.reason: Graphene lacks complete canonical write sets, immutable authorized wave plans, per-resource fences, expected versions, and commit-time claimant validation
